root_causes.description: The recommendation service pod consumes an anomalous amount of CPU during the incident window (mean 2.343 cores, p95/p99 ~3.60, peak 3.608), ~33x higher than frontend (0.070) and ~94x higher than product-catalog (0.025). Error rate, memory usage, restarts, error logs, error traces and pod events all remain at baseline, which is the exact signature of an injected CPU-stress fault rather than a crash, latency, memory or dependency failure.

evidence.expected_baseline: peer services frontend 0.070 cores / product-catalog 0.025 cores; recommendation baseline ~0.05 cores
recommendation 2.343 cores mean in same window (~33x higher)
recommendation 2.343 cores mean in same window (~94x higher)
no error logs expected for cpu_stress
no error traces expected for cpu_stress
no OOMKilled/BackOff/restart events expected for cpu_stress

root_causes.description: CPU starvation on the recommendation pod could secondarily inflate request latency, but no latency or error signal was observed and the dominant anomaly is clearly CPU, making this a weaker explanation.

evidence.expected_baseline: a latency fault would surface slow/error traces and a p99 latency spike
latency fault degrades successful throughput; no such signal observed

root_causes.description: recommendation calls product-catalog downstream, so a slow/failing product-catalog could propagate upstream; however product-catalog CPU is healthy (0.025 cores) and recommendation error rate is 0, showing no downstream degradation.

evidence.expected_baseline: healthy baseline; no downstream resource pressure
dependency_failure would raise upstream error rate; not observed

remediation_steps: Confirm the CPU saturation source on the recommendation pod: kubectl top pods -n otel-demo and inspect for a stress-ng / busy-loop sidecar or injected fault marked seed42.
If the fault is injected, stop/disable the CPU-stress experiment targeting recommendation (remove the chaos/fault injection).
Verify recommendation CPU returns to baseline (~0.05 cores) with sum(rate(container_cpu_usage_seconds_total{namespace="otel-demo",pod=~"recommendation-.*"}[2m])).
If no injection is present, apply CPU limits/requests and HPA to recommendation to bound runaway CPU, then re-check error_rate and p99 latency for secondary customer impact.
